top_signal.title: Young entrepreneur seeking advice
top_signal.summary: I wanted to get your advice on something as a young 26 years old entrepreneur.   I'm currently selling my services below market rates, which has helped me attract clients, but I'm finding it difficult to scale the business.   I've been advised to increase my pricing, so I experimented by raising my rates to 2–3 times the original price. However, for the next four months, I didn't manage to acquire a single client.   It makes me question whether my skill set is strong enough to compete at higher prices or whether I simply don't have the financial resources to hire A-players who can help take the business to the next level.   Right now, I'm stuck between offering cheaper services with low client retention and working with B-level talent, or charging higher rates but struggling to convince clients of the value.   How would you approach scaling a business in this situation? Would you focus on improving the team, positioning, pricing, or something else entirely?   I'd genuinely appreciate your perspective and advice.       submitted by     /u/Federal-Work1613       [link]       [comments]
